signals.title: AUD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Crowded Long Unwind
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7017, breaking cleanly below its SMA200 at 0.7024 alongside the SMA20 and SMA50 at 0.7148 and 0.7095. The G10 currency strength scorecard registers a massive 1.809% spread between leader USD (+1.109%, n=9 pairs) and laggard AUD (-0.699%, n=4 pairs). CFTC data shows Leveraged Funds net long AUD at +59,299 contracts, sitting at the 97th percentile (z=+2.11) of its 52-week range. While the nominal policy rate spread favors AUD with RBA at 4.35% versus Fed at 4.00% (-35bp carry advantage to AUD), surging US yields and bear flattening across the US curve have accelerated speculative liquidation. Options markets confirm downside pressure with the 1-month 25d Risk Reversal printing -0.95 in favor of puts. The combination of an extreme G10 performance divergence and crowded speculative positioning leaves AUD vulnerable to an extended long squeeze. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, positioning unwind dominating rate support. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 September — hike bias priced. Risk: Spot recovers and closes above the SMA200 at 0.7024, arresting the positioning squeeze.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Intervention Friction vs Carry Dominance
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.42, maintaining support above its moving-average cluster of SMA20 at 156.54, SMA50 at 158.70, and SMA200 at 158.45. Fed policy at 4.00% versus BoJ at 1.25% provides an authoritative 275bp carry premium favoring USD, keeping structural dips shallow. Verbal warnings from Japanese Finance Minister Katayama, citing summit discussions with Trump regarding Yen weakness, introduce explicit headline risk below 160.00. However, VIX trades at 15.7 (normal volatility), confirming cross-asset panic is absent and safe-haven JPY demand is not active. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds flipped net long JPY to +20,069 contracts (95th percentile, z=+1.57), while options demand reflects severe downside hedging via a 25d Risk Reversal of -2.26. Carry demand sustains spot until actual intervention is executed or US yields reverse. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-driven upside capped by official intervention risk. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 30 October — hold priced. Risk: Coordinated physical currency intervention pushes spot below the SMA20 at 156.54.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Macro Yield Divergence vs Retail Extreme
signals.text: USD/CAD holds at 1.4149, trading firmly above its SMA20 at 1.3915, SMA50 at 1.3945, and SMA200 at 1.3840. The Fed at 4.00% versus BoC at 2.25% delivers a +175bp carry premium supporting the USD, reinforced by a 10Y sovereign yield gap of -120bp against Canadian debt. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment registers an extreme short stance at 87% short (13% long), directly fading the institutional trend while CFTC Leveraged Funds maintain a net short CAD exposure of -41,404 contracts (26th percentile). With WTI crude retreating -1.54% to $93.2 and the US 2-year yield surging to 4.850%, fundamental and rate drivers continue to punish the Canadian Dollar. Retail traders attempting to pick the top face severe squeeze risk as the pair trends higher. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD, structural carry and retail contrarian tailwind. Catalyst: BoC meeting 28 October — hike bias priced. Risk: Retail sentiment flips balanced and spot breaks below the SMA20 support at 1.3915.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Yield Spread Widening + Options Skew
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1374, pinned beneath its moving-average cluster of SMA20 at 1.1548, SMA50 at 1.1539, and SMA200 at 1.1626. The policy rate divergence between Fed at 4.00% and ECB at 2.65% generates a 135bp carry advantage favoring the Dollar, while the 10-year Bund-Treasury spread sits wide at -160bp. German and Spanish labor data beats failed to lift the common currency against a broader bear flattener in the US yield curve. FX options display steady hedging demand against EUR weakness, with the 1-month 25d Risk Reversal printing -0.81 for base puts. Leveraged Funds remain net short EUR by -51,355 contracts (32nd percentile), showing institutional positioning remains aligned with the structural downtrend. The technical barrier formed by the moving averages limits recovery attempts to corrective bounces. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, rate spread widening capping relief rallies. Catalyst: US Durable Goods Orders at 12:30 UTC. Risk: A daily close back above the SMA50 at 1.1539 neutralizes immediate downside momentum.
